channel.title: Greenlight time?
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Greenlight time?" - The indigenous American Coyote character escapes to his own metanarrative properties, and the Foundation seeks to stop him from spreading to other folklore.

item.title: Re: Greenlight time?
item.content:encoded:
Awesome, thank you for the quick reply!
I think I can keep this an interesting SCP proper, given some nice hefty changes. How do these changes sound:

1. Yes, on reflection I think there's no reason the Serpent's Hand needs to get involved (maybe they'll take an interest in a tale or somethin, or that interaction will just stay in my own headcanon).

2. However, I think the Chaos Insurgency still fits pretty well, and "Coyote" would definitely gravitate to them over the Foundation. But perhaps this turn of events works best as the final note?

3. Time to simplify the plot. Remove SH involvement, and go into less detail about the anthropologist character and how the Foundation discovered the SCP.

4. However, I'm not sure whether to remove the Foundation's attempted first contact (If I do keep it, I think I can rework it to make their method more interesting). If I keep it, it can open the storytelling opportunity for the next "file" to be a report of Coyote's betrayal and realignment with the CI. But of course, just cutting all that out would majorly simplify things.

Basically, I'm not sure whether it's acceptable for the most recent development to be Coyote "joining" the CI (and therefore being currently uncontained). Or perhaps the Foundation just throws resources at it via cultural suppression and weaken him so much that he stops being a problem (or so they think). That second ending might warrant an Ethics Committee log.

How do those changes and proposals sound?
Thank you, I really appreciate the feedback, I do want to make a good article.

item.title: Re: Greenlight time?
item.content:encoded:
1) The reviewers are major sticklers on the 400-word limit. Also, you're going to need to collapse it down using the following string: [G[collapsible]G] collapsed text [G[/collapsible]G] (just eliminate the Gs and put a lot of text in place of the "collapsed text" part (check the wiki text quick reference under the box for more information).

+ show block
– hide block

2) The big problem you have is that Coyote has already escaped into the metanarrative in the real world (he's featured in the White Wolf Werewolf: The Apocalypse as a major spirit as well as a number of webcomics and other media, such as the American Gods books and even Marvel Comics). It's hard to keep a good trickster contained.

3) Keep in mind also that as a trickster, and one that's been doing it for aeons, Coyote will find a loophole, assuming it's not a bluff to keep attention over here as he does something over there. Out of all of the various deities you could mess with, this is one of the trickier ones simply because Coyote is known for his schemes.

Ironically, that makes him a good pick for this, but there has to be a reason for him to behave other than his personal honor.

4) This would be better for Tales than as an article. Also, I'm sort of worried about the "tragic" tag; Coyote just doesn't do tragedy. He generally comes out on top and making fun of all of those involved, sometimes even himself. That The Foundation has handled gods is worth noting, especially in this case.

5) The Chaos Insurgency and Serpent's Hand are mutually antagonistic, both between themselves and The Foundation. While it appears that's allowed for with CI, it's unlikely that SH would help The Foundation. Also, as SH hates to contain entities, especially humanoid ones, I'm not sure that they would agree to do so themselves, especially one as potentially powerful as Coyote.

6) Overall, I think you may be trying to do too much with this, and you may want to break it down a little. You have a couple of different things going on, and any one of them (sapient stories, a character from myth, even a deity branching out) would be great to focus on. I'm just not sure one entry would do it justice.

item.title: Greenlight time?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mostly an exploration of a cool idea

Page Layout: Bog-standard SCP format

Elevator Pitch: The set of Indigenous American stories about Coyote are an anomalous set of living narrative and metanarrative characteristics, which the Foundation worries might "jump" into other contemporary narratives. "Coyote" fools the Foundation and involves the Chaos Insurgency

Central Narrative: There is definitely a plot to this, but I hope you'll find it interesting enough to warrant such a big explanation:

+ show block
– hide block

A culture's practices and beliefs determine its stories, right? But what if the stories start to have a mind (or agenda) of their own? A Foundation anthropologist reports that the set of stories about Coyote acts differently from any other set of stories about a character (indigenous or otherwise); specifically, the stories and the overall set itself shares Coyote's characteristics, as well as some instinct for self preservation and an unknown degree of sapience. This worries the Foundation, who are concerned about what would happen if Coyote discovers how to (or maybe just decides to) jump into other contemporary narrative-sets. They have no idea what will happen in that scenario.

A year later, Foundation web-sweeper bots detect a set of movie concepts, novel plots, and fanfiction arcs, many involving birds of some kind, which overall "behaved like a narrative animal, but with more personality", similarly to the Coyote set. The foundation at first classifies this as a new, similar SCP, but the anthropologist later realizes that it is in fact a containment breach, where "Coyote took the form of a bird". The site is taken down, and it is discovered that many of the original posts were made by the teenage daughter of a former member of the Chaos Insurgency of Kootenai descent.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Foundation deals with a metanarrative SCP and gets hoodwinked. The Chaos Insurgency gets involved.

Additional Notes: The most important thing I want to watch out for is that I don't mis-portray parts of any Native American culture(s). That being said, this very much isn't the mythical figure of Coyote as an SCP (that'd be both stupid and impossible to write), but is a conscious set of stories which act similar to the character they portray. The point is to look at how the foundation will handle an SCP like this, and vice versa…
